stemMd: When a magnesium atom becomes Mg²⁺, what changes?

options.label: B
options.textMd: It loses two neutrons and no electrons.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Its nucleus splits into two equal nuclei.

options.label: D
options.textMd: It loses two electrons while its proton number stays unchanged.

explanationMd: A +2 charge means there are two fewer electrons than protons. Magnesium forms the ion by losing two electrons; its nucleus remains magnesium. Distinguishing electron transfer from nuclear changes avoids confusing ions with isotopes or new elements.

distractorRationale.e: Changing proton number would create a different element.
distractorRationale.a: Electron gain would make the charge negative.
distractorRationale.b: Neutron loss does not generate a +2 charge.
distractorRationale.c: Ordinary ion formation is not nuclear fission.
